title: [CQ-R13c2] Wrapper fail-closed protected runtime paths
description:
Objective: when the JetBrains launcher marks a session protected (MOE_RUNTIME_PROTECTED=1, from CQ-R13c1), both agent wrappers use exactly MOE_PROXY_PATH and MOE_DAEMON_PATH or refuse to start. They never fall back to their own root's packages or to the global install. Without the marker, the wrappers keep today's fallback exactly, preserving legacy policy. This is CQ-R01's follow-up 6.

Split out of CQ-R13 (task-f4811a72) by architect-e4b7eee0 on 2026-10-30. It depends on CQ-V08b (task-7f82e200), which also edits moe-agent.sh, moe-agent.ps1 and the postflight harness, so these edits land after it. It is file-disjoint from CQ-R13c1, and the env contract is pinned in both rows.

Today:
- moe-agent.sh uses PROXY_PATH_OVERRIDE and DAEMON_PATH_OVERRIDE only when the file exists (`-f`). Otherwise it falls back to its own root, then the global install (~line 716 and ~1563).
- moe-agent.ps1 uses $env:MOE_PROXY_PATH (~459) and $env:MOE_DAEMON_PATH (~599), then $PSScriptRoot\.., then Get-MoeInstallPath.

Deliverable:
- With MOE_RUNTIME_PROTECTED exactly '1', each wrapper requires both variables to be non-empty, absolute paths to regular files. Otherwise it exits non-zero before writing any MCP config or starting any daemon or CLI.
- The refusal uses one fixed code in both launchers, MOE_RUNTIME_PROTECTED_PATH_MISSING, plus a one-line message that names the failing variable, never the path.
- Any other value of MOE_RUNTIME_PROTECTED counts as unset (legacy), and legacy behavior stays byte-identical.
- Tests in scripts/tests/postflight.sh and scripts/tests/postflight.ps1, daemon-free like the harness's other wrapper rows:
  - protected with a missing proxy path, and protected with a missing daemon path, are both refused with the code, with no fallback taken;
  - protected with both files present proceeds;
  - unset keeps today's fallback.
- scripts/tests/parity-check.sh still passes, with the new code and variable name in both launchers.

Out of scope:
- the JetBrains marker (CQ-R13c1);
- the other R01 follow-ups;
- VS Code;
- .moe edits.

Verification command (fresh, exit 0 required): bash scripts/tests/postflight.sh && bash scripts/tests/parity-check.sh. Also run the PowerShell harness, scripts/tests/postflight.ps1, through powershell.exe, or record that it is unavailable.
definitionOfDone: With MOE_RUNTIME_PROTECTED=1, moe-agent.sh and moe-agent.ps1 start only with absolute, existing MOE_PROXY_PATH and MOE_DAEMON_PATH files. Otherwise each exits with MOE_RUNTIME_PROTECTED_PATH_MISSING before any MCP config, daemon or CLI start, and never uses its own root or the global install. Shown by harness tests.
Without the marker, or with any other value, both wrappers keep today's fallback order unchanged. Shown by harness tests.
parity-check.sh passes with the new code and variable present in both launchers.
The verification command exits 0 with its output supplied to complete_task.
taskRails: No direct .moe edits; no Git-write commands by agents; wrappers own landing.
Do not enable verified-local or claim isolation until all requisite implementation and certification gates pass.

implementationPlan.description:
TESTS FIRST (red), scripts/tests/postflight.sh. Load test-driven-development.

Ordering: this row becomes claimable only after CQ-V08b (task-7f82e200) and CQ-V04c (task-c4e076cd) are DONE, and both edit all four files of this plan. Re-read the landed bytes and anchor on names, never on line numbers.

Contract, pinned with CQ-R13c1 (landed in 71092fa):
- The JetBrains launcher sets MOE_RUNTIME_PROTECTED to exactly '1', beside MOE_PROXY_PATH and MOE_DAEMON_PATH.
- The refusal is one line on stderr, byte-identical in both wrappers, followed by exit code 1:
  [ERROR] MOE_RUNTIME_PROTECTED_PATH_MISSING: <VAR> must be an absolute path to an existing file when MOE_RUNTIME_PROTECTED=1; refusing to start.
- <VAR> is MOE_PROXY_PATH or MOE_DAEMON_PATH, checked in that order. The value is never printed.

Add one section, `[protected runtime]`, just before `echo "PASS postflight.sh"`, with the comment `Twin: postflight.ps1.` Keep it compact (target 90 lines or fewer; see the size budget in planningNotes): one setup block, one row helper and eight rows.

Setup, under PR="$TMP_DIR/protected":
- PRJ="$PR/project", with .moe/project.json (autoCommit false) and an empty .moe/messages/chan-general.jsonl, as in the [team join] row.
- A marks file, "$PR/marks". Every fixture appends one line to it.
- "$PR/marked-proxy.js": one prefix line that appends 'protected-proxy' to the marks file, followed by the bytes of "$FAKE_PROXY". Build it with `{ printf ...; cat "$FAKE_PROXY"; } > "$PR/marked-proxy.js"`. parity-check.sh fails on any redirect INTO $FAKE_PROXY and on any embedded fake-proxy body, so never write to $FAKE_PROXY and never copy its request-parsing line into the harness.
- "$PR/fake-daemon.js": appends `protected-daemon <its argv after the script>` to the marks file, then writes "<value after --project>/.moe/daemon.json" as {port: 9876, pid: process.ppid, startedAt, projectPath}. process.ppid is the wrapper, which stays alive, so the wrapper's start poll accepts it.
- Decoys for every legacy fallback. Each appends a 'decoy-...' line:
  - "$PR/bin/moe-proxy" records 'decoy-proxy', then runs `exec node "$FAKE_PROXY" "$@"`, so a legacy run still works;
  - "$PR/bin/moe-daemon" records, then exits 1;
  - a global install at "$PR/install", named by "$PR/home/.moe/config.json" {"installPath": ...}. Its packages/moe-daemon/dist/index.js and packages/moe-proxy/dist/index.js each record, then exit 1.
- A regular file, "$PRJ/rel-proxy.js", and a directory, "$PR/dir.js".

Row helper: pr_run ROW MARKER PROXY DAEMON [extra wrapper args...].
- First reset "$PR/marks", "$PRJ/.mcp.json", "$PRJ/.moe/daemon.json" and "$PR/home/.config".
- MARKER '-' means unset; any other value is exported as given.
- Run from a subshell whose cwd is "$PRJ", with PATH="$PR/bin:$TMP_DIR:$PATH" HOME="$PR/home" MOE_PROXY_PATH=PROXY MOE_DAEMON_PATH=DAEMON FAKE_CLAIM_MODE=idle MOE_TASKLESS_WAIT_SEC=5 MOE_DISABLE_HEARTBEAT=1:
  timeout "${POSTFLIGHT_TIMEOUT_SEC}s" "$WRAPPER" --project "$PRJ" --worker-id worker-protected --role worker --command /bin/true --no-loop "$@"
- Send the output to "$PR/ROW.out". Keep the exit code under set +e / set -e, as the other rows do.

Each REFUSED row asserts all of:
- the exit code is exactly 1;
- an output line contains `MOE_RUNTIME_PROTECTED_PATH_MISSING: <VAR> must be`;
- the output does not contain the PROXY or DAEMON value under test (skip this check for the empty value);
- "$PR/marks" does not exist: no proxy, daemon or decoy ran;
- neither "$PRJ/.mcp.json" nor "$PR/home/.config/claude/mcp_servers.json" exists.

Rows:
- P1: marker '1', proxy "$PR/missing/proxy.js", daemon "$PR/fake-daemon.js". Refused, naming MOE_PROXY_PATH.
- P2: marker '1', proxy "$PR/marked-proxy.js", daemon "$PR/missing/daemon.js". Refused, naming MOE_DAEMON_PATH.
- P3: marker '1', proxy 'rel-proxy.js' (it exists relative to the cwd, but it is not absolute). Refused, naming MOE_PROXY_PATH.
- P4: marker '1', daemon "$PR/dir.js" (a directory). Refused, naming MOE_DAEMON_PATH.
- P5: marker '1', proxy '' (set but empty). Refused, naming MOE_PROXY_PATH.
- P6: marker '1', both paths valid, no --no-start-daemon, and no daemon.json. It proceeds:
  - no refusal code;
  - marks contains `protected-daemon start --project $PRJ` and `protected-proxy`, and no `decoy` line;
  - "$PRJ/.mcp.json" mcpServers.moe.args equals ["$PR/marked-proxy.js"] (read it with node or python).
- P7: marker unset, proxy "$PR/missing/proxy.js", with --no-start-daemon. It keeps today's fallback:
  - no refusal code;
  - marks contains `decoy-proxy`;
  - .mcp.json mcpServers.moe.command is 'moe-proxy'.
- P8: marker '01', proxy "$PR/marked-proxy.js", daemon "$PR/missing/daemon.js", with --no-start-daemon. It stays legacy, because only exactly '1' protects:
  - no refusal code;
  - marks contains `protected-proxy`.

RED proof, using a trimmed scratch harness (mem:convention-postflight-scratch-harness):
- Copy scripts/ into a snapshot directory on /mnt/d (mem:gotcha-shared-tree-long-harness-needs-snapshot).
- Build x-scratch.sh from postflight.sh's prelude, up to and including the line that copies postflight-fake-proxy.js to $FAKE_PROXY (re-grep for it), then the new section, then a PASS line.

implementationPlan.description:
GREEN, scripts/moe-agent.sh.

Never edit this file while any harness or wrapper from this checkout is running: live seats hot-reload it. Run `bash -n scripts/moe-agent.sh` before every save of a final version (mem:gotcha-editing-wrapper-while-harness-runs).

1. Next to PROXY_PATH_OVERRIDE and DAEMON_PATH_OVERRIDE at the top, set RUNTIME_PROTECTED to 1 only when "${MOE_RUNTIME_PROTECTED:-}" = 1 (string equality); otherwise 0.
   - Write it as an if/else. The file runs under set -e, so no bare `[ ] && X=1` (mem:gotcha-moe-agent-sh-set-e-unguarded-assignments).
   - Add a short comment naming CQ-R13c2 and the JetBrains contract.
2. Add a function, refuse_unprotected_runtime VAR. It prints the step-1 refusal line to stderr, with the ${RED}[ERROR]${NC} prefix other errors use, then exits 1. It never prints the value.
3. The gate. Place it after the project checks and `export MOE_WORKER_ID`, and before `ensure_mcp_config` is defined or called. It then runs before any MCP config write, daemon start, proxy RPC or CLI.
   When RUNTIME_PROTECTED=1, check PROXY_PATH_OVERRIDE, then DAEMON_PATH_OVERRIDE:
   - a value is absolute if it matches `/*`, or the drive form `[A-Za-z]:[\\/]*` (Git Bash);
   - refuse unless the value is absolute and `[ -f ]` holds.
   In legacy mode the gate prints nothing.
4. No fallback at the use sites. This closes the window after the gate: a file that vanishes later is refused, not replaced.
   - In ensure_mcp_config, right after the override branch and before `command -v moe-proxy`, add `elif [ "$RUNTIME_PROTECTED" = 1 ]; then refuse_unprotected_runtime MOE_PROXY_PATH`.
   - Add the same to the daemon autostart, before `command -v moe-daemon`, naming MOE_DAEMON_PATH.
   - Leave TEAM_PROXY's own-root and global fallbacks unchanged. They are unreachable under protection, because PROXY_ARGS is always set.
5. Legacy lines stay byte-identical. Make additions only, and do not reformat the existing fallback chains.

Error handling: guard every new command for set -e. The refusal is the only new output.

Run the step-1 scratch harness against this wrapper. All eight rows must pass.

- refuse_unprotected_runtime VAR: printf '%b[ERROR]%b %s\n' "$RED" "$NC" "<sentence>" >&2, then exit 1. The value is never printed.
- require_protected_runtime_file VAR VALUE: case /*|[A-Za-z]:[\\/]*) [ -f ] && return 0, else refuse.
- The gate runs right after `export MOE_WORKER_ID`, before ensure_mcp_config is defined, and checks the proxy, then the daemon.

TESTS FIRST (red), scripts/tests/postflight.ps1. Add the twin `[protected runtime]` section just before `Write-Host 'PASS postflight.ps1'`, with the comment `Twin: the [protected runtime] case in postflight.sh.` Use the same eight rows, the same assertions and the same marks lines. Keep it compact (target 110 lines or fewer).

Differences from the sh twin:
- Env: rows set it on the harness process, and Invoke-WrapperProcess inherits it. Save and restore, in a finally, every variable the rows touch: MOE_RUNTIME_PROTECTED, MOE_PROXY_PATH, MOE_DAEMON_PATH, USERPROFILE, TEMP, TMP, FAKE_CLAIM_MODE, MOE_TASKLESS_WAIT_SEC and MOE_DISABLE_HEARTBEAT.
- P5: in PowerShell, `$env:X = ''` deletes X (mem:gotcha-powershell-empty-env-var-deletes). So P5 is "MOE_PROXY_PATH unset", which the wrapper treats exactly like empty.
- Wrapper args: -Project, -WorkerId worker-protected, -Role worker, -Command $trueCmd and -NoLoop, plus -NoStartDaemon for P7 and P8.
- Decoys: the decoy global install is named by "$USERPROFILE\.moe\config.json" (Get-MoeInstallPath). The ps1 has no PATH fallback, so there is no bin decoy. The install's packages\moe-proxy\dist\index.js decoy records 'decoy-proxy' and then carries the fake-proxy bytes, so P7 runs. P7 asserts that marks has 'decoy-proxy': today's ps1 order goes from a set-but-missing MOE_PROXY_PATH straight to the global install.
- No project .mcp.json: the ps1 MCP config is a temp file. P6 therefore proves the proxy through the 'protected-proxy' mark and the absence of any decoy mark.
- Refused rows also run with TEMP and TMP pointed at an empty per-row directory, and assert that it holds no moe-mcp-config-* file afterwards.
- P3: wrap the run in Push-Location "$prProject" (Start-Process starts the child in the current location), so 'rel-proxy.js' exists relative to the wrapper's cwd. Pop-Location in a finally.
- P6: the fake daemon writes process.ppid as its pid, which is the wrapper's PowerShell (the Start-Process parent). If that parent is not the wrapper on this engine, keep the fake daemon alive for up to 10 s instead, and say why.
- Building the marked proxy without tripping parity-check:
  - read it with `$proxyBody = [IO.File]::ReadAllText($fakeProxy)`, on its own line;
  - write it with `[IO.File]::WriteAllText($prMarkedProxy, $prefix + $proxyBody)`;
  - never put Set-Content, Add-Content or Out-File on a line that names $fakeProxy, and never pass $fakeProxy as the first argument of WriteAll*.
- Quote paths into generated JS with ConvertTo-Json, as the daemon.json fixtures above do.
- Save the file with the UTF-8 BOM and LF endings it has now.

implementationPlan.description:
GREEN, scripts/moe-agent.ps1. This is the exact twin of step 2. Keep its UTF-8 BOM (parity-check fails without it) and its LF endings.

1. Place the new code after `$env:GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT = '0'` and before `$script:MoeDeregistered` and the PowerShell.Exiting registration. A refusal there cannot run Invoke-MoeDeregister through an unset proxy.
   - Set `$script:MoeRuntimeProtected = ($env:MOE_RUNTIME_PROTECTED -ceq '1')`, with the same comment as the sh twin.
   - Add a function, Stop-MoeProtectedRuntime([string]$Name). It writes the step-1 refusal line, with an `[ERROR] ` prefix and no color codes, through [Console]::Error.WriteLine, then runs `exit 1`. That exits the script pass, and the supervisor at the top of the file re-exits with 1.
2. The gate. When protected, check 'MOE_PROXY_PATH', then 'MOE_DAEMON_PATH':
   - take the value with the same .Trim('"') the legacy reads apply;
   - a value is absolute if it matches `^[A-Za-z]:[\\/]` or the UNC form `^[\\/]{2}[^\\/]`, or, only on a non-Windows pwsh ($PSVersionTable.PSEdition -eq 'Core' -and -not $IsWindows), if it starts with '/' by an Ordinal StartsWith;
   - refuse unless the value is absolute and `Test-Path -LiteralPath $v -PathType Leaf` holds;
   - do not use IsPathFullyQualified: PowerShell 5.1 does not have it.
3. No fallback at the use sites.
   - Insert `if ($script:MoeRuntimeProtected) { Stop-MoeProtectedRuntime 'MOE_PROXY_PATH' }` as the FIRST statement inside both proxy fallback branches: `if (-not $proxyScript) {` (own root), and the `if (-not (Test-Path $proxyScript)) {` that falls back to Get-MoeInstallPath.
   - Do the same inside the two $daemonScript fallback branches, naming 'MOE_DAEMON_PATH'.
   - Leave the legacy lines otherwise untouched.

Error handling: the file sets $ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop', so do not use Write-Error for the refusal. It would throw instead of exiting 1 with one line.

Run the step-3 trimmed ps1 harness against this wrapper; all eight rows must pass. If powershell.exe is unreachable, at least parse the file with [System.Management.Automation.Language.Parser]::ParseFile under pwsh or powershell (mem:pattern-ps1-function-probe-via-ast), and record which engine ran.
implementationPlan.note:
moe-agent.ps1 +23/-0, additions only. BOM kept, LF, ParseFile 0 errors.
- After `$env:GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT = '0'`, before $script:MoeDeregistered and the PowerShell.Exiting registration: `$script:MoeRuntimeProtected = ($env:MOE_RUNTIME_PROTECTED -ceq '1')`, plus the same comment as the sh twin.
- Stop-MoeProtectedRuntime([string]$Name) writes "[ERROR] <sentence>" via [Console]::Error.WriteLine, then `exit 1`. No Write-Error.
- The gate checks MOE_PROXY_PATH, then MOE_DAEMON_PATH:
  - the value is taken with .Trim('"');
  - absolute = `^[A-Za-z]:[\\/]` or UNC `^[\\/]{2}[^\\/]`, or '/' by an Ordinal StartsWith only on non-Windows Core;
  - the -and short-circuits, so Test-Path -LiteralPath -PathType Leaf never sees an empty value.
  - The loop variables are uniquely named ($moeProtected*) so script scope is not clobbered.
- `if ($script:MoeRuntimeProtected) { Stop-MoeProtectedRuntime '<VAR>' }` is the FIRST statement in the 4 fallback branches: the proxy own-root and the global-install fallback, and the daemon own-root and the global-install fallback. The error-exit blocks are untouched.

1. Mutants. Every one is killed.
   sh, rows run one at a time:
   - (a) no gate: P2 P3 P4 red. P1 and P5 stay green because the ensure_mcp_config use-site refuses them; VPk proves that use-site is load-bearing.

   - (i) no moe_call_allowed in cleanup_temp: P9.
   - (j) no WORKER_ID clear: P2 P3 P4.
   - Vanish injection: deleting the proxy after the gate (VP) refuses MOE_PROXY_PATH with nothing run; VP plus no use-site (VPk) is red. The daemon pair behaves the same: VD refuses, VD plus no use-site (VDl) runs decoy-daemon and is red.

   ps1 under PS 5.1:
   - (a) P2 P3 P4.
   - (b) P3 P5.
   - (c) no Leaf: P4.
   - (d) P2 P4.
   - (e) P8.
   - (f) gate after the MCP temp config: P2 P3 P4.
   - (g) P1-P5.
   - (h) Get-MoeInstallPath first: P6 P8 P9.
   - Vanish injection: VP and VD make P6 refuse the right variable with empty marks. VPk runs decoy-proxy and VDl runs decoy-install-moe-daemon.
   - Unmutated copy: green.
2. Resolution paths.
   - sh: TEAM_PROXY, moe_rpc, the heartbeat (via moe_rpc) and the codex/gemini/grok TOML/JSON writers all come from PROXY_CMD/PROXY_ARGS. ensure_mcp_config either sets those to the override or refuses.
   - ps1: Invoke-MoeRpc(Raw), the TOML writers and Start-HeartbeatSidecar all use $proxyScript, and the daemon uses $daemonScript, each override-or-refuse.
   - moe-call.sh was the only self-resolving helper; it is now guarded.
   - On a ps1 use-site exit, Invoke-MoeRpc (line 1509) is not yet defined, so the Exiting handler runs no RPC.
3. Legacy.
   - Every hunk is an addition gated on RUNTIME_PROTECTED/$script:MoeRuntimeProtected. The only changes to existing lines are the two sh moe-call `if` lines; with the marker off, moe_call_allowed is always true.
   - No new names collide with existing ones.
   - P7 (unset) and P8 ('01') plus the whole legacy postflight suite are green (step 5).
4. Edge cases.
   - The sh case pattern accepts /x, C:\x, C:/x and //srv/x, and rejects C:x, x and ''. A backslash UNC is refused in sh only, which fails closed; ps1 accepts UNC.
   - A quoted value is trimmed identically in the ps1 gate and resolver.
   - A symlink to a file passes, which is accepted.
   - A hot reload re-execs (sh) or reruns the file (ps1), so the gate reruns from the same env.

executionContract.intendedBehavior: With MOE_RUNTIME_PROTECTED exactly '1', scripts/moe-agent.sh and scripts/moe-agent.ps1 run only the proxy and daemon files that MOE_PROXY_PATH and MOE_DAEMON_PATH name. Each must be an absolute path to an existing regular file, checked before any MCP config, daemon, proxy RPC or CLI start. Otherwise the wrapper prints one MOE_RUNTIME_PROTECTED_PATH_MISSING line that names the variable, never its value, and exits 1. It never falls back to PATH, its own packages or the global install, even when a file vanishes after the check. Any other marker value keeps today's behavior byte-identical.
acceptanceCriteria: Protected with a missing, relative, directory or empty MOE_PROXY_PATH: refused with exit 1 and the code naming MOE_PROXY_PATH. No MCP config is written and no proxy, daemon or decoy runs.
Protected with a missing or directory MOE_DAEMON_PATH: refused the same way, naming MOE_DAEMON_PATH.
Protected with both files valid: the daemon starts from exactly MOE_DAEMON_PATH and every RPC goes through exactly MOE_PROXY_PATH; no decoy fallback runs.
Marker unset: a missing MOE_PROXY_PATH still takes today's fallback (sh: moe-proxy on PATH; ps1: the global install).
parity-check.sh passes, and both launchers contain MOE_RUNTIME_PROTECTED and MOE_RUNTIME_PROTECTED_PATH_MISSING.
invariants: Legacy output and fallback order are unchanged.
The refusal never prints a path value.
The code, the variable name and the refusal sentence are spelled identically in both wrappers.
No change to the JetBrains marker (CQ-R13c1), VS Code, the daemon or .moe.
compatibility: Every existing postflight row (all legacy) passes unchanged.
The legacy MOE_PROXY_PATH/MOE_DAEMON_PATH semantics are unchanged: sh uses the value if `-f` holds, else falls back; ps1 trims quotes, then falls back.
approvedScope: moe-agent.sh: RUNTIME_PROTECTED, refuse_unprotected_runtime, the pre-ensure_mcp_config gate, and the elif refusals in ensure_mcp_config and the daemon autostart

moe-agent.ps1: $script:MoeRuntimeProtected, Stop-MoeProtectedRuntime, the gate before the PowerShell.Exiting registration, and first-statement refusals in the $proxyScript/$daemonScript fallback branches

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
Chosen: one early gate per wrapper, plus a refusal at each use-site fallback.
- The gate refuses before any MCP config write, daemon start, proxy RPC or CLI.
- The use-site refusal closes the window in which a protected file vanishes after the gate. That window is the scenario CQ-R13c1's description names.

Rejected:
- A gate only: a file deleted between the gate and its use would still fall back to PATH, the wrapper's own root or the global install.
- Use-site refusals only: the MCP config is written before the daemon site is reached, and DoD 1 says the refusal comes before any MCP config.
- Rewriting the legacy fallback chains under an if/else: the re-indentation inflates the diff against QA's 400-line cap and risks legacy drift. Additive elif and first-statement guards keep the legacy lines byte-identical.
- Editing parity-check.{sh,ps1} to list the new code: its auto families are prefix-scoped (MOE_COMMIT_/ATTR_/CHECKPOINT_/ATTRIBUTION_/ACCOUNT_), the task text says it 'still passes', and both harness rows already pin the code and variable spelling in each launcher. That keeps the plan at 4 files.
- A docs edit: no doc names MOE_PROXY_PATH or MOE_DAEMON_PATH today, and CQ-R13 owns the epic docs sweep. A comment was left on CQ-R13 instead.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
- sh proxy: resolved once, in ensure_mcp_config (PROXY_CMD/PROXY_ARGS). The order is the override if `-f`, then `command -v moe-proxy`, then $ROOT_DIR/packages/moe-proxy/dist/index.js, then get_moe_install_path. The codex/gemini/grok TOML writers, TEAM_PROXY, moe_rpc and the heartbeat all reuse PROXY_ARGS/PROXY_CMD.
- sh daemon: resolved in the autostart block, in the same order, with `command -v moe-daemon`.
- ps1: a single $proxyScript is used everywhere downstream: the MCP temp config, the TOML writers, Invoke-MoeRpc and Start-HeartbeatSidecar.
  - Its order: $env:MOE_PROXY_PATH with .Trim('"'); if empty, $PSScriptRoot\..; if Test-Path fails, Get-MoeInstallPath ($env:USERPROFILE\.moe\config.json); otherwise Write-Error and exit 1.
  - $daemonScript does the same at the autostart.
- ps1 registers PowerShell.Exiting -> Invoke-MoeDeregister before it resolves the proxy, so the gate must come before that registration.
- moe-agent.sh runs under set -e. moe-agent.ps1 needs its UTF-8 BOM. Both files are LF.
- JetBrains: selectProtectedAgentRuntime (TerminalAgentLauncher.kt) sets the three variables. WSL launches pass /mnt/ paths through toWslPath, so sh sees POSIX absolute paths and ps1 sees drive paths.
- Harness: rows run the real wrapper with the fake proxy (postflight-fake-proxy.js), --no-start-daemon and --no-loop. parity-check forbids redirects into $FAKE_PROXY/$fakeProxy and any embedded proxy body.
- Run times: the full postflight.sh takes 12 minutes or more on WSL; postflight.ps1 takes about 10-12 minutes via powershell.exe.
planningNotes.risks:
1) Contested files and order. CQ-V07, CQ-V08, CQ-V08b and CQ-V04c all edit these four files. I added CQ-V04c (task-c4e076cd) to this row's dependsOn, per the epic rail on serializing overlapping affectedFiles, so this row is claimed after both. Line numbers will have moved; re-read the files.
2) Never edit moe-agent.sh while a harness or wrapper from this checkout is running. Live seats hot-reload it, so run `bash -n` before saving.
3) QA's 400 net-line cap includes tests. Target 40 runtime lines or fewer per wrapper, and 90 (sh) and 110 (ps1) harness lines or fewer. Use a row helper, not copy-pasted rows.
4) Harness runs launched from WSL into Windows leak MOE_*/CLAUDE_* env and fail from a /tmp cwd. Use the /mnt/d scratch recipe.
5) PowerShell cannot hold an empty env var, so P5 is 'unset' in the ps1 twin.
6) Under $ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop', a refusal through Write-Error throws instead of exiting 1.
7) A legacy regression in the gate would brick every seat. The existing rows (all legacy), plus P7 and P8, are that guard.
